name: Open-delta voltage transformer connection
summary: Two phase-to-phase VTs connected in V to provide all three line voltages without a neutral reference.
description: The open-delta or V-V connection uses two double-pole VTs connected between phases, sharing one phase as a common point. It gives all three line-to-line secondary voltages at lower cost than three VTs and is common in MV metering and switchgear where neutral voltages are not needed.

Because there is no neutral reference, phase-to-neutral voltages and zero-sequence voltage cannot be measured. Earth-fault directional elements or meters needing phase-to-neutral inputs therefore cannot be fed from this connection, which the reader must check against the relay requirements.
readingNotes: Identify the common phase shared by both VTs.
Check that no connected device needs phase-to-neutral voltage.
drawingChecklist: Show both VTs and common phase
distinction: An open-delta connection uses two phase-to-phase VTs; a broken-delta winding uses three earthed VTs for residual voltage.
